data.description:
## Context

The brainstorm pipeline has a structural blind spot for cemented premises in spec content itself. During the understanding loop, the LLM pattern-completes the user's request and silently inserts load-bearing premises about content sources, data shape, user model, and trust boundaries. Every downstream layer (gap analysis, scenario red team, fidelity reviewers) operates on the resulting spec text and inherits those premises, so the pipeline cannot currently catch this class of gap. Motivating case: an "English to Spanish translation" brainstorm shipped a spec that never surfaced where Spanish content would come from, conflating storage (locale JSON files) with sourcing (DeepL, Google, AI batch, human translator). This epic targets premises that live inside the spec's prose — complementary to c183-ed2a (Adversarial review of inference-sourced decisions), which targets the structured-decision channel via decision_id tracking. c183-ed2a hardens the structured channel; this epic hardens the prose channel.

## Success Criteria

- SC1. Translation replay: A fresh /dso:brainstorm "translate from English to Spanish" run surfaces the Spanish-content sourcing decision before approval — via gap-analysis inference-signal scan triggering re-entry to Socratic dialogue, OR via inferred-source structural marker bolded at approval gate, OR via assumption-category Step 1 fire.
- SC2. No-input feature replay: A synthetic refactor / hook-fix / infra-only brainstorm completes Phase 1 with the Inputs bullet stating "no external inputs" — verified by gap-analysis Read/Grep against proposed code paths confirming no external input handling logic.
- SC3. Decision-tree calibration replay: Synthetic brainstorm cases verify the inverted decision tree across 7 sub-cases — (a) Inputs-and-data with out-of-scope content sourcing fires at Step 1; (b) cross-SC reference via verbatim phrase match in an explicit SC suppresses at Step 3; (c) cross-SC reference covered only by an inferred SC does NOT suppress (circular closed); (d) reference to existing repo file/service suppresses at Step 2; (e) reference to deprecated/legacy file fires at Step 2; (f) conventional default at specific-claim level for established domain suppresses at Step 4; (g) conventional default with no domain established fires at Step 4 (default-fire on unknown).
- SC4. Schema, marker, and rendering integration: category enum in red-team output schema includes "assumption" and matches sub-bullet category names; structural marker <<inferred:source-name>> documented; renderer converts markers to bold at approval gate; bold rendering rule placed inline with approval-gate render step in phases/approval-gate.md.
- SC5. Cross-file structural consistency: All changes ship as a single coordinated change set verified by structural test validating BOTH static presence AND semantic alignment — Inputs row in Tell-Me-More table; non-optional Inputs bullet in Understanding Summary template; gap-analysis inference-signal scan with extended word list and 5-second timeout in epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md Part B; structural-marker convention; inverted 4-step decision tree in scenario-red-team.md with co-located scope parentheticals (Step 3 parenthetical revised); schema enum update; bold rendering rule co-located with approval-gate step.
- SC6. SC Gap Check fallback and severity-floor non-regression: A synthetic NFR-style assumption finding (latency-tier or cost-tier premise) that doesn't map to a user-outcome SC surfaces under a Premise to confirm line at the SC Gap Check prompt with confirm/revise/accept-risk options. Structural test asserts no severity filter is applied to assumption findings between blue-team output and approval-gate rendering.

## Dependencies

None.

## Approach

Defense-in-depth via coordinated prompt-level changes designed to ground LLM behavior in observable evidence rather than self-judgment. Four design principles emerged from two passes of bot-psychologist scrutiny: mandatory observable actions over judgment; fire-first over suppress-first; explicit structural markers over text-match; always-on bullets over omit-if-N/A. Eight changes ship together: (1) Inputs dimension in Phase 1 Tell-Me-More table; (2) non-optional Inputs bullet in Understanding Summary with two permitted values (explicit source / "no external inputs"); (3) gap-analysis inference-signal scan with extended trigger list and MUST-execute Read/Grep verification (5-second timeout); (4) provenance propagation via structural marker <<inferred:source-name>>; (5) inverted 4-step decision tree in scenario-red-team.md (Step 1 fires Inputs-and-data; Step 2 requires verified true to suppress; Step 3 requires verbatim match in explicit SC; Step 4 requires specific-claim conventional default with established domain); (6) co-located scope parentheticals; (7) bold rendering rule placed inline with approval-gate step; (8) SC Gap Check fallback Premise to confirm line for unmappable findings.

## Scenario Analysis

8 surviving scenarios (15 raw → 8 after blue-team filtering); all addressed by the approach above:

- Read/Grep timeout on large repos (high, runtime): mitigated by 5-second timeout with treat-as-not-verifiable-and-fire fallback.
- Trigger word paraphrases beyond extended list (high, runtime): mitigated by multi-layer defense — Step 1 mandatory verification catches paraphrased premises that escape the inference-signal scan.
- Step 1 suppression on stale repo state (high, runtime): mitigated by qualifying "verified true" to active/non-deprecated code; matches in deprecated/test/legacy directories fire.
- Step 3 cross-SC suppression circular (high, runtime): mitigated by requiring verbatim match in explicit or confirmed-via-gap-question SC; inferred SCs alone do not suppress.
- Schema/instruction non-atomic deployment (high, deployment): mitigated by SC5 single-coordinated-change-set requirement.
- Structural test static-only (medium, deployment): mitigated by SC5 semantic alignment requirement.
- "Stated domain" undefined (high, configuration): mitigated by definition (= Context section's user/business context); absent → default-fire.
- No severity floor protection (medium, configuration): mitigated by SC6 structural test asserting no severity filter applied between blue-team output and approval-gate rendering.

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2.6): not triggered
  - Bright-line conditions that fired: none
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered — re-triggered after spec revision
  - Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 8 (15 raw → 8 surviving across two scrutiny passes; second pass filtered 7 scenarios as resolved by third-pass design changes)
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none (re-runs were skill-driven post-revision, not user-requested via approval gate)
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (epic modifies brainstorm SKILL.md, epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md, scenario-red-team.md, phases/approval-gate.md, phases/post-scrutiny-handlers.md). Bot-psychologist re-review applied with PROVEN_PROPOSING_FIX verdict; all five proposed fixes incorporated (mandatory tool-call language; fire-first decision-tree inversion; structural markers replacing text-match; specific-claim conventional-default check; co-located bold rendering rule).
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (no volume decision; tooling change to brainstorm pipeline itself)

## Out of Scope

- New agent dispatch (no premise-auditor agent; reuses existing red/blue scenario mechanism)
- Schema changes beyond category enum addition
- Blue-team prompt changes (existing filter rubric covers assumption category as-is)
- Config knobs to force-enable/disable Inputs dimension
- Concurrent brainstorm session handling
- Per-project trigger-word-list extension
- Changes to dso:red-team-reviewer agent (different agent, owned by c183-ed2a)
- PRECONDITIONS event tracking or decision_id infrastructure (owned by 736d-b957 and c183-ed2a)
data.title: Catch cemented-premise gaps in brainstorm via Inputs dimension and assumption-category red team finding
